chapter: Music in Harlem: records, radio, gigs
title: Hearing live music in Harlem: Cotton Club, Savoy Ballroom, Dizzy
summary: He recalls passing the Cotton Club and later hearing Dizzy Gillespie at the Savoy before it closed.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: You mentioned the Apollo Theater. Certainly you would have heard live music there, and you mentioned the club where you saw the photo of Louis Jordan outside.
So, what other places would you have gone to hear live music when you were really starting to get serious about music?
Were there other places in the neighborhood?

There were places. Well, when I was really young there, well...you see Harlem was a place that, especially at that time, I mean there was music everywhere. There were a lot of–of course, I was too young. I mean, in the 30’s I was, you know, a little boy going to school. But we used to pass by The Cotton Club, the famous Cotton Club on the way going to school, you know. The Savoy Ballroom...uh, which I actually was able, I grew up enough to go to the, The Savoy before it closed, you know.
Did you see any of the “Battle of the Bands?”

Uh, no. I went to, when I went to The Savoy, I went there, Dizzy Gillespie was there. And that was uh we were really into Dizzy, so, I was still fairly young. I was in my uh early teens, you know, when I went to The Savoy, and it wasn’t long after that The Savoy uh closed, you know. So, I didn’t see these “Battle of the Bands,” but I heard a lot about them, but I didn’t witness them myself.
